domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on training M2 via reinforcement learning with expert developers as reward models and perturbation pipelines for agent generalization, which is post-training methodology. M2 is designed for coding and workplace agentic tasks with in-house expert developers shaping model behavior for developer workflows. The content covers post-training RL with reward models and perturbation pipelines plus deployment results on OpenRouter and downloads. Requires familiarity with RL, reward models, and agent scaffolds but remains accessible to practitioners. Published as a 14-minute conference-style presentation on the AI Engineer channel. All key claims are directly stated in the transcript with supporting evidence anchors.

summary: Olive Song introduces MiniMax M2, an open-weight model with 10 billion active parameters designed for coding, workplace agentic tasks, and cost efficiency. MiniMax distinguishes itself by developing both foundation models and applications in-house, giving researchers direct access to expert developers who serve as reward models during training. M2 ranks top among open-source models on intelligence and agent benchmarks, achieved the most downloads in its first week, and reached top three token usage on OpenRouter. The presentation details four key characteristics. First, code experience is supported by scaled environments and scaled experts, using real internet data and reinforcement learning to train a full-stack multilingual model, with in-house expert developers providing precise reward and evaluation on problem definition, bug fixing, and repo refactoring. Second, long-horizon state tracking uses interleaved thinking, where the model interleaves thinking with tool calling across tens to 100 turns within a single user interaction, enabling adaptation to noisy, dynamic environments and workflow automation across tools like Gmail, Notion, and terminal. Third, robust generalization to agent scaffolds is achieved through perturbation pipelines across the model's operational space—tool information, system prompts, user prompts, chat templates, environments, and tool responses—after discovering that tool scaling alone was insufficient. Fourth, multi-agent scalability is enabled by M2's small size and cost effectiveness, allowing parallel copies to handle research, analysis, reporting, and front-end illustration simultaneously. Future directions include M2.1 and M3, with focus on better coding, memory, context management, proactive AI for workplace, vertical experts, and integration with MiniMax's audio and video generation models. MiniMax seeks community feedback and is committed to sharing developments openly.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and MiniMax Overview
sections.summary: Olive Song introduces herself as a researcher studying reinforcement learning and model evaluation at MiniMax. MiniMax is a global company developing both foundation models and applications, including multimodality models, video generation (Hailuo), speech and music generation, and in-house agent applications. This dual focus gives researchers firsthand experience with developer needs.

sections.title: M2 Model Introduction and Benchmark Performance
sections.summary: M2 is introduced as an open-weight model with 10 billion active parameters designed for coding, workplace agentic tasks, and cost efficiency. It ranks top among open-source models on intelligence and agent benchmarks, achieved the most downloads in its first week, and reached top three token usage on OpenRouter.

sections.title: Code Experience: Scaled Environments and Expert Developers
sections.summary: M2's code experience is supported by scaled environments and scaled experts. Real internet data and reinforcement learning train a full-stack multilingual model. In-house expert developers participate in the training cycle, providing precise reward and evaluation on problem definition, bug fixing, and repo refactoring, identifying behaviors developers enjoy and trust.

sections.title: Long-Horizon State Tracking: Interleaved Thinking
sections.summary: M2 handles long-horizon tasks using interleaved thinking, interleaving thinking with tool calling across tens to 100 turns within a single user interaction. This enables adaptation to noisy, dynamic environments and workflow automation across tools like Gmail, Notion, and terminal with minimal human intervention. A stock market trading illustration demonstrates stability despite environment perturbations.

sections.title: Robust Generalization to Agent Scaffolds
sections.summary: Agent generalization is defined as adaptation to perturbations across the model's entire operational space. Tool scaling alone was insufficient; perturbing agent scaffolds caused failures. MiniMax designed perturbation pipelines across tool information, system prompts, user prompts, chat templates, environments, and tool responses to ensure generalization.

sections.title: Multi-Agent Scalability and Future Directions
sections.summary: M2's small size and cost effectiveness enable multi-agent scalability, demonstrated with parallel copies handling research, analysis, reporting, and front-end illustration. Future plans include M2.1 and M3 with focus on better coding, memory, context management, proactive AI, vertical experts, and integration with audio and video generation models. MiniMax seeks community feedback and commits to sharing developments openly.
